title: UCLA, UC Berkeley Freeze Internship Permits After Trump Tightens CPT Rules for International Students
excerpt: A federal memo restricts Curricular Practical Training to mandatory coursework only, threatening a key work pathway for hundreds of thousands of F-1 visa holders
body:
• The Department of Homeland Security issued an August 24 memo restricting Curricular Practical Training (CPT) to programs where the training is mandatory for all students, effectively blocking elective-course-based internship authorizations.
  • UCLA and UC Berkeley have paused certain CPT applications, with Berkeley saying it is unlikely to process some work authorization requests "in the near future." The University of Illinois has also tightened requirements.
  • The restriction compounds earlier proposed rules that would eliminate Day 1 CPT and impose fixed terms on F-1 student visas, threatening a pathway used by hundreds of thousands of Indian students and tech workers.

The University of California, Los Angeles and the University of California, Berkeley have frozen certain internship work authorizations for international students after the Trump administration issued a federal memo tightening rules for Curricular Practical Training — a work pathway used heavily by Indian students in the United States.

The memo, dated August 24 and issued by the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) under Immigration and Customs Enforcement, warned that the agency has "observed a rise in Curricular Practical Training authorizations that appear to violate regulatory requirements which permit CPT only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum."

The directive came with a blunt threat: "Failure to comply with SEVP regulations may result in an institution losing certification to enroll foreign students."

Universities Move to Comply

The response from major universities was swift. UCLA confirmed it has "paused certain Curricular Practical Training authorizations while it reviews recent federal guidance and determines next steps."

https://x.com/KTVU/status/2093030828792070534

UC Berkeley's international office went further, describing the August 24 memo as "more narrow in focus, more direct, and includes content that is more restrictive in nature" compared to an earlier mid-August memo. The office said it is unlikely to process certain work authorization applications "in the near future" and urged international students to plan accordingly.

The University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign announced that effective immediately, it will only approve CPT "where participation by all students in the program is mandatory for graduation." Applicants must now provide evidence that their CPT employer has entered into a cooperative agreement with the university.

Previously approved and authorized CPT will not be affected, the universities said.

What Changed

The core restriction narrows CPT eligibility to programs where the practical training is required for all students in that curriculum, regardless of citizenship. CPT tied to elective courses — previously a common route for international students to gain work experience — can no longer be approved.

Universities said they will continue processing "degree-requirement" CPT as normal and plan to resume processing doctoral dissertation and master's thesis research CPT after consulting with legal experts.

"Nothing about these regulations has changed. However, schools and employers should consider themselves on notice: under President Trump, abuse of this generous system will no longer be tolerated."

— Department of Homeland Security statement

A Wider Crackdown on Student Work Pathways

The CPT restriction is the latest in a series of moves targeting work pathways for international students. The Department of Homeland Security finalized rules last month that would eliminate open-ended stays for F-1 visa holders, impose fixed visa terms, and block students from enrolling in programs at the same or lower degree level — changes that would effectively shut down the "Day 1 CPT" pathway used by many Indian tech workers to maintain work authorization between H-1B lottery attempts.

Day 1 CPT allows F-1 students to begin working immediately after starting a graduate program related to their field. Many Indian professionals enrolled in such programs specifically to maintain their work eligibility while awaiting H-1B results — a practice the new rules would block.

"This is a strategy that employers have been able to push off on to their employees," said Danielle Goldman, co-founder and CEO of Build Talent Labs. "For larger, risk-averse institutions, Day 1 CPT has been something that is a responsibility of the foreign national versus them having to do anything."

Impact on Indian Students

Indian nationals account for the largest share of F-1 student visa holders pursuing STEM graduate degrees in the United States. The combined effect of the CPT restrictions and the proposed F-1 rule changes threatens to disrupt career planning for hundreds of thousands of students and professionals who rely on these pathways for practical work experience and continued employment.

Students currently on valid CPT authorizations are not affected, but those planning to apply for elective-course-based internships will need to explore alternative arrangements or reconsider their academic and career strategies in the United States.
